items.fr: Mon fils apprend son vocabulaire tous les soirs avant le dîner.
items.en: My son learns his vocabulary every evening before dinner.
items.ipa: mɔ̃ fis a.pʁɑ̃ sɔ̃ vɔ.ka.by.lɛʁ tu le swaʁ a.vɑ̃ lə di.ne
items.notes: "dîner" keeps the circumflex on the i in the traditional spelling.

items.fr: Les élèves ont écouté attentivement la nouvelle enseignante.
items.en: The students listened attentively to the new teacher.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃.t‿e.ku.te a.tɑ̃.ti.vmɑ̃ la nu.vɛl ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃t
items.notes: There are two links here, and "ont" before "écouté" is said ɔ̃t.

items.fr: depuis deux heures
items.en: for two hours, and still going
items.respell: duh-PWEE duh ZUHR
items.notes: The same two hours as the row above and the other end left open.

items.fr: Le professeur a noté sept fautes dans ma dictée.
items.en: The teacher noted seven mistakes in my dictation.
items.ipa: lə pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ a nɔ.te sɛt fot dɑ̃ ma dik.te
items.notes: "sept" is said with its final t, unlike "cent".

items.fr: Nous avons rempli le formulaire pour la classe de francisation.
items.en: We filled out the form for the francization class.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁɑ̃.pli lə fɔʁ.my.lɛʁ puʁ la klas də fʁɑ̃.si.za.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "francisation" takes a c, not an s, whatever the sound suggests.

items.fr: L'agent a vérifié l'orthographe de son nom sur le certificat.
items.en: The clerk checked the spelling of his name on the certificate.
items.ipa: l‿a.ʒɑ̃ a ve.ʁi.fje l‿ɔʁ.tɔ.gʁaf də sɔ̃ nɔ̃ syʁ lə sɛʁ.ti.fi.ka
items.notes: "orthographe" is written with an h after the t, and it is often left out.

items.fr: Le conseil scolaire a envoyé un avis aux familles cette semaine.
items.en: The school board sent a notice to families this week.
items.ipa: lə kɔ̃.sɛj sko.lɛʁ a ɑ̃.vwa.je œ̃.n‿a.vi o fa.mij sɛt sə.mɛn
items.notes: "conseil" ends in -eil. Do not confuse it with "conseille".

items.fr: Les enfants ont chanté ensemble pendant la fête de fin d'année.
items.en: The children sang together during the end-of-year party.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃.te ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la fɛt də fɛ̃ da.ne
items.notes: The link between "enfants" and "ont" is said as a z.

items.fr: Le directeur a reçu une lettre du conseil scolaire ce matin.
items.en: The principal received a letter from the school board this morning.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ a ʁə.sy yn lɛtʁ dy kɔ̃.sɛj sko.lɛʁ sə ma.tɛ̃
items.notes: "reçu" takes a cedilla under the c before the u, to keep the s sound.

items.fr: J'ai révisé mes verbes irréguliers avant l'examen oral.
items.en: I reviewed my irregular verbs before the oral exam.
items.ipa: ʒe ʁe.vi.ze me vɛʁb i.ʁe.gy.lje a.vɑ̃ l‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ ɔ.ʁal
items.notes: "irréguliers" takes two r, and one is often dropped.

items.fr: Les élèves ont applaudi leur professeur le dernier jour d'école.
items.en: The students applauded their teacher on the last day of school.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃.t‿a.plo.di lœʁ pʁɔ.fɛ.sœʁ lə dɛʁ.nje ʒuʁ de.kɔl
items.notes: "applaudi" takes two p, and writing one is a common mistake.

items.fr: Ma collègue a suivi une formation continue le week-end dernier.
items.en: My colleague took a continuing-education course last weekend.
items.ipa: ma kɔ.lɛg a sɥi.vi yn fɔʁ.ma.sjɔ̃ kɔ̃.ti.ny lə wik.ɛnd dɛʁ.nje
items.notes: "week-end" keeps its English spelling, with a hyphen in French.

items.fr: Nous avons demandé une attestation officielle après le stage.
items.en: We requested an official attestation after the internship.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ də.mɑ̃.de yn a.tɛs.ta.sjɔ̃ ɔ.fi.sjɛl a.pʁɛ lə staʒ
items.notes: "officielle" takes two f and ends in -ielle, not -ièle.

items.fr: Les parents ont assisté à la remise des diplômes samedi.
items.en: The parents attended the diploma ceremony on Saturday.
items.ipa: le pa.ʁɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃.t‿a.sis.te a la ʁə.miz de di.plom sam.di
items.notes: "assisté" takes two s to hold the s sound between vowels.

items.fr: J'ai vérifié l'horaire des examens sur le site de l'école.
items.en: I checked the exam schedule on the school's website.
items.ipa: ʒe ve.ʁi.fje l‿ɔ.ʁɛʁ de.z‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ syʁ lə sit də l‿e.kɔl
items.notes: "horaire" starts with a silent h, which allows the elision.

items.fr: L'enseignant a noté nos progrès dans le carnet de suivi.
items.en: The teacher noted our progress in the tracking booklet.
items.ipa: l‿ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃ a nɔ.te no pʁɔ.gʁɛ dɑ̃ lə kaʁ.nɛ də sɥi.vi
items.notes: "progrès" ends in a silent s, like "après".

items.fr: Nous avons choisi un tuteur pour aider notre fils en lecture.
items.en: We chose a tutor to help our son with reading.
items.ipa: nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʃwa.zi œ̃ ty.tœʁ puʁ ɛ.de nɔtʁ fis ɑ̃ lɛk.tyʁ
items.notes: "choisi" loses the t of "choisit" in the passé composé. Keep the two forms apart.

items.fr: La secrétaire a remis le certificat directement aux parents.
items.en: The secretary handed the certificate directly to the parents.
items.ipa: la sə.kʁe.tɛʁ a ʁə.mi lə sɛʁ.ti.fi.ka di.ʁɛk.tə.mɑ̃ o pa.ʁɑ̃
items.notes: "secrétaire" takes an acute accent then a grave one, and the two are often mixed up.

items.fr: Les élèves ont appris un nouveau poème pour la fête de l'école.
items.en: The students learned a new poem for the school celebration.
items.ipa: le.z‿e.lɛv ɔ̃.t‿a.pʁi œ̃ nu.vo pɔ.ɛm puʁ la fɛt də l‿e.kɔl
items.notes: "poème" takes a grave accent on the e, not a circumflex.

items.fr: en une heure
items.en: in an hour, that is how long it takes
items.respell: AHⁿ NÜN UHR
items.notes: The fifth card of a set the corpus published four fifths of.

items.fr: Le directeur adjoint surveille la cour pendant la récréation.
items.en: The vice principal watches the yard during recess.
items.ipa: lə di.ʁɛk.tœʁ ad.ʒwɛ̃ syʁ.vɛj la kuʁ pɑ̃.dɑ̃ la ʁe.kʁe.a.sjɔ̃
items.notes: "adjoint" ends in -oint. Keep the silent t in writing.

items.fr: J'ai signé le registre d'absence à l'accueil de l'école.
items.en: I signed the absence register at the school's front desk.
items.ipa: ʒe si.ɲe lə ʁə.ʒistʁ dab.sɑ̃s a l‿a.kœj də l‿e.kɔl
items.notes: "accueil" takes two c and is said a-keuille, not ak-seuille.

items.fr: Les enseignants ont préparé un examen commun pour tous les élèves.
items.en: The teachers prepared a common exam for all the students.
items.ipa: le.z‿ɑ̃.sɛ.ɲɑ̃.z‿ɔ̃ pʁe.pa.ʁe œ̃.n‿ɛg.za.mɛ̃ kɔ.mœ̃ puʁ tu le.z‿e.lɛv
items.notes: "commun" takes two m. Do not confuse it with "comment".

items.fr: L'élève a demandé la permission de sortir de la classe.
items.en: The student asked for permission to leave the classroom.
items.ipa: l‿e.lɛv a də.mɑ̃.de la pɛʁ.mi.sjɔ̃ də sɔʁ.tiʁ də la klas
items.notes: "permission" takes two s to hold the s sound between vowels.

items.fr: J'habite ici depuis trois ans.
items.en: I have lived here for three years.
items.respell: zha-BEET ee-SEE duh-PWEE trwah-ZAHⁿ
items.notes: The sentence the whole lesson exists to produce. The English is a perfect and the French is a present, and nothing in the French moves.

items.fr: Il y a un problème.
items.en: There is a problem.
items.respell: eel ee ah uhⁿ proh-BLEM
items.notes: A thing behind it, so the three words mean there is.

items.fr: Il y a deux jours.
items.en: Two days ago.
items.respell: eel ee ah duh ZHOOR
items.notes: A measurement behind it and nothing after that, so the same three words mean ago. No verb in it at all, which is why it can be here.

items.fr: Je vais partir.
items.en: I am going to leave.
items.respell: zhuh veh par-TEER
items.notes: Aller in the present and the naming form behind it, untouched.

items.fr: Il y a une heure de retard.
items.en: There is an hour of delay.
items.ipa: /il i a yn œʁ də ʁə.taʁ/
items.respell: eel ee ah ün UHR duh ruh-TAR
items.notes: The sharp one. Four words in common with « il y a une heure » and the fifth turns the hour back into a thing. This is why the rule is about the full stop and not about the noun.

items.fr: Tu vas partir.
items.en: You are going to leave.
items.respell: tü vah par-TEER
items.notes: The person moved and the second verb did not.

items.fr: Il va partir.
items.en: He is going to leave.
items.respell: eel vah par-TEER
items.notes: The shortest of the six, ten letters, and the one the dictée uses for the pair because its negative also fits.

items.fr: Tu vas travailler ce soir ?
items.en: Are you going to work tonight?
items.respell: tü vah trah-vah-YAY suh SWAR
items.notes: Her question, and every word in it is one the learner has had since lesson 1 in A2. The answer is one word longer than the question.

items.fr: Je ne vais pas travailler.
items.en: No, I am not going to work.
items.respell: zhuh nuh veh pah trah-vah-YAY
items.notes: What he meant, in full. Twenty letters, so it is not a dictée target either.

items.fr: Ah, d'accord. À ce soir, alors.
items.en: Ah, all right. See you tonight, then.
items.respell: ah da-KOR · a suh SWAR ah-LOR
items.notes: She books him in, cheerfully, on the strength of a sentence that was correct. Nobody corrected anything, so nothing was learned and he is now expected.

items.fr: Tu vas faire quoi ce soir ?
items.en: What are you going to do tonight?
items.respell: tü vah FEHR kwah suh SWAR
items.notes: The commonest question in the language after « ça va ? », and it is this construction with a question word dropped into the slot.

items.fr: Nous allons partir.
items.en: We are going to leave.
items.respell: noo za-lohⁿ par-TEER
items.notes: The liaison pulls a z across into allons and the nasal survives it.

items.fr: Le film que tout le monde recommande sort vendredi.
items.en: The film everybody recommends comes out on Friday.
items.ipa: /lə film kə tu lə mɔ̃d ʁə.kɔ.mɑ̃d sɔʁ vɑ̃.dʁə.di/
items.respell: luh FEELM kuh too luh mohⁿd ruh-koh-MAHⁿD · sor vahⁿ-druh-DEE

items.fr: Ils vont partir.
items.en: They are going to leave.
items.respell: eel vohⁿ par-TEER
items.notes: The plural of the form the singular already had, and partir has still not moved.

items.fr: Tu ne vas pas partir.
items.en: You are not going to leave.
items.respell: tü nuh vah pah par-TEER

items.fr: Il ne va pas partir.
items.en: He is not going to leave.
items.respell: eel nuh vah pah par-TEER
items.notes: The pair with row 503 is the one the dictée runs, because both halves of it fit.

items.fr: Je ne vais pas partir.
items.en: I am not going to leave.
items.respell: zhuh nuh veh pah par-TEER
items.notes: In the futur proche the negative wraps aller, not the verb after it: ne vais pas partir.

items.fr: Vous allez partir.
items.en: You are going to leave. (to more than one person, or politely)
items.respell: voo za-lay par-TEER
items.notes: The same liaison, and the ending nobody hears any difference in.

items.fr: Je vais pas sortir.
items.en: I am not going to go out. (spoken French, with the ne dropped)
items.respell: zhuh veh pah sor-TEER
items.notes: THE ONE RECEPTIVE ROW. Fifteen letters, so the dictée COULD take it and must not: lesson 21 in A1 introduced the dropped ne for reception only and produces it nowhere. No voiceflash, no dictation, no typed answer, and one ear question.

items.fr: Je vais manger avec des amis.
items.en: I am going to eat with friends.
items.respell: zhuh veh mahⁿ-ZHAY ah-VEK day-za-MEE
items.notes: A plan with something after the naming form, which nothing about the rule minds.

items.fr: Tu vas venir avec nous samedi ?
items.en: Are you going to come with us on Saturday?
items.respell: tü vah vuh-NEER ah-VEK noo sam-DEE
items.notes: The invitation, with the day on the end. Samedi rather than the weekend, which is respelled four different ways in this corpus and is nobody's decision to make here.

items.fr: Nous n'allons pas partir.
items.en: We are not going to leave.
items.respell: noo na-lohⁿ pah par-TEER
items.notes: The ne elides in front of the vowel and the liaison z goes with it: noo na-lohⁿ, not noo za-lohⁿ.

items.fr: Vous n'allez pas partir.
items.en: You are not going to leave. (to more than one person, or politely)
items.respell: voo na-lay pah par-TEER
items.notes: The same elision and the same lost liaison.

items.fr: Ils ne vont pas partir.
items.en: They are not going to leave.
items.respell: eel nuh vohⁿ pah par-TEER
items.notes: Six persons, one position for the two halves, and the naming form has not moved once.

items.fr: Je vais payer.
items.en: I am going to pay.
items.respell: zhuh veh pay-YAY
items.notes: The same naming form as lesson 7's own card « Je peux payer. », behind a different first verb.

items.fr: Tu vas travailler demain.
items.en: You are going to work tomorrow.
items.respell: tü vah trah-vah-YAY duh-MAⁿ
items.notes: A four-syllable naming form, and the slot does not care. Twenty-one letters, so no dictée.

items.fr: Je ne vais pas manger de viande ce soir.
items.en: I'm not going to eat meat tonight.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə vɛ pa mɑ̃.ʒe də vjɑ̃d sə swaʁ/
items.respell: zhuh nuh veh pah mahⁿ-ZHAY duh VYAHⁿD suh SWAR
items.notes: After the negation, de la viande shortens to de viande, losing the article.

items.fr: Elle ne va pas finir le rapport ce soir.
items.en: She isn't going to finish the report tonight.
items.ipa: /ɛl nə va pa fi.niʁ lə ʁa.pɔʁ sə swaʁ/
items.respell: ehl nuh va pah fee-NEER luh ra-POR suh SWAR
items.notes: Rapport doubles its p in spelling though it is pronounced as a single consonant.

items.fr: Je ne vais pas sortir ce soir.
items.en: I am not going to go out tonight.
items.respell: zhuh nuh veh pah sor-TEER suh SWAR
items.notes: In futur proche, ne and pas wrap around the conjugated verb aller, right before the infinitive.

items.fr: Il y a un problème avec l'eau chaude dans la salle de bain.
items.en: There is a problem with the hot water in the bathroom.
items.ipa: il i a œ̃ pʁɔ.blɛm a.vɛk lo ʃod dɑ̃ la sal də bɛ̃
items.notes: "bain" ends in a silent nasal n. Do not add a final e.

items.fr: Le musée n'ouvre que le mardi.
items.en: The museum only opens on Tuesdays.
items.respell: luh mü-ZAY noovr kuh luh mar-DEE

items.fr: J'ai parlé.
items.en: I spoke.
items.respell: zhay par-LAY
items.notes: The -ER group, and lesson 1's own headline verb. An -ER naming form ends in -er and its past form ends in -é, and those are the same sound.

items.fr: Il a fini.
items.en: He finished.
items.respell: eel ah fee-NEE
items.notes: The -IR group, and lesson 3's own frame verb. « Il a fini. » beside that lesson's « Il finit tôt. » is one verb in two tenses with the same three letters in front.

items.fr: Il a vendu.
items.en: He sold.
items.respell: eel ah vahⁿ-DÜ
items.notes: The -RE group, and lesson 4's own frame verb. The naming form loses its -re and takes -u, and this is the only one of the three where the ending is not already on the naming form somewhere.

items.fr: Nous avons choisi.
items.en: We chose.
items.respell: noo za-vohⁿ shwah-ZEE
items.notes: A second -IR verb, in another person, so the ending is clearly the group and not the verb.

items.fr: Nous n'avons pas mangé.
items.en: We did not eat.
items.respell: noo na-vohⁿ pa mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: The negative wraps avoir, and the liaison z goes with it: noo na, not noo za.

items.fr: J'ai mangé.
items.en: I ate. / I have eaten.
items.respell: zhay mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: One English form covers both of these and French has one form for both, which is the piece of luck in this lesson.

items.fr: Tu as mangé.
items.en: You ate.
items.respell: tü ah mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: The person moved and the past form did not.

items.fr: Nous avons mangé.
items.en: We ate.
items.respell: noo za-vohⁿ mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: The liaison pulls a z across into avons and the nasal survives it.

items.fr: Vous avez mangé.
items.en: You ate. (to more than one person, or politely)
items.respell: voo za-vay mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: The same liaison.

items.fr: Je n'ai pas mangé.
items.en: I did not eat.
items.respell: zhuh nay pa mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: Lesson 15 in A2 could not test je at all: « Je ne vais pas partir. » is seventeen. Ne shortens to n' in front of avoir and that is the whole difference.

items.fr: Tu n'as pas mangé.
items.en: You did not eat.
items.respell: tü na pa mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: The ne has shortened again, and it does that in front of every single form of avoir.

items.fr: Il a mangé.
items.en: He ate.
items.respell: eel ah mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: Manger takes avoir, and the past form is mangé.

items.fr: Elle est revenue lundi.
items.en: She came back on Monday.
items.respell: ehl eh ruhv-NÜ luhⁿ-DEE

items.fr: Je ne suis pas allé au bureau.
items.en: I did not go to the office.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə sɥi pa za.le o by.ʁo/
items.respell: zhuh nuh swee pah zah-LAY oh bü-ROH

items.fr: Ils ont mangé.
items.en: They ate.
items.respell: eel zohⁿ mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: Eleven letters, and the liaison again. Six persons and the second word has not moved once.

items.fr: Ils n'ont pas mangé.
items.en: They did not eat.
items.respell: eel nohⁿ pa mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: Six persons, one gap, and the past form has stayed outside it every time.

items.fr: Et Marie, elle est venue ?
items.en: And Marie, did she come?
items.respell: ay mah-REE, ehl eh vuh-NÜ

items.fr: Non, elle n’est pas venue.
items.en: No, she did not come.
items.respell: nohⁿ, ehl neh pah vuh-NÜ

items.fr: Il est entré sans frapper.
items.en: He came in without knocking.
items.respell: eel eh tahⁿ-TRAY sahⁿ frah-PAY

items.fr: Ils sont retournés en France.
items.en: They went back to France.
items.respell: eel sohⁿ ruh-toor-NAY ahⁿ FRAHⁿSS

items.fr: Elle est descendue à midi.
items.en: She came down at midday.
items.respell: ehl eh day-sahⁿ-DÜ ah mee-DEE

items.fr: Le verre est tombé.
items.en: The glass fell.
items.respell: luh VEHR eh tohⁿ-BAY

items.fr: Nous sommes passés devant chez toi.
items.en: We went past your place.
items.respell: noo somm pah-SAY duh-VAHⁿ shay TWAH

items.fr: Il est devenu professeur.
items.en: He became a teacher.
items.respell: eel eh duhv-NÜ proh-feh-SUHR

items.fr: Elles sont reparties lundi.
items.en: They left again on Monday.
items.respell: ehl sohⁿ ruh-pahr-TEE luhⁿ-DEE

items.fr: Vous n'avez pas mangé.
items.en: You did not eat. (to more than one person, or politely)
items.respell: voo na-vay pa mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: Seventeen letters, one over. The same lost liaison.

items.fr: Elle a bien répondu.
items.en: She answered well.
items.respell: ehl ah byehⁿ ray-pohⁿ-DÜ
items.notes: And the same word in the same place on an -RE verb.

items.fr: Je vais manger.
items.en: I am going to eat.
items.respell: zhuh veh mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: Lesson 15's construction, in the frame verb, so the pair with row 541 differs by one syllable and by nothing else.

items.fr: J'ai travaillé hier.
items.en: I worked yesterday.
items.respell: zhay trah-vah-YAY YEHR
items.notes: Hier is the commonest past time word in the language, and it sits on the end.

items.fr: Nous avons beaucoup travaillé.
items.en: We worked a lot.
items.respell: noo za-vohⁿ boh-KOO trah-vah-YAY
items.notes: A three-syllable adverb, still in the gap. Twenty-six letters, so no dictée.

items.fr: Il a fini la semaine dernière.
items.en: He finished last week.
items.respell: eel ah fee-NEE lah suh-MEN dehr-NYEHR
items.notes: Finir gives fini. La semaine dernière puts it in the past.

items.fr: Tu as parlé avant-hier ?
items.en: Did you speak the day before yesterday?
items.respell: tü ah par-LAY ah-vahⁿ-TYEHR
items.notes: A question with no inversion and no est-ce que, which is lesson 22 in A1's register point and the way it is actually said.

items.fr: Il va manger.
items.en: He is going to eat.
items.respell: eel va mahⁿ-ZHAY
items.notes: And the same pair with il in front, where the two little words are va and a and neither of them is stressed.

items.fr: On a mangé il y a une heure.
items.en: We ate an hour ago.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ na mɑ̃.ʒe il i a yn œʁ/
items.respell: ohⁿ na mahⁿ-ZHAY eel ee ah ün UHR
items.notes: The loop lesson 14 in A2 asked for. On rather than nous, which is lesson 1 in A2's rule for the whole level.

items.fr: J'ai mangé une pomme.
items.en: I ate an apple.
items.respell: zhay mahⁿ-ZHAY ün POM
items.notes: THE OBJECT DOES NOT GO IN THE GAP. It goes after the past form, like everything that is not a small word, and this is the row that makes the rule true rather than nearly true.

items.fr: Elle a mangé une pomme.
items.en: She ate an apple.
items.respell: ehl ah mahⁿ-ZHAY ün POM
items.notes: A feminine subject, a feminine object, and mangé has not moved a letter. With avoir there is no agreement here at all.

items.fr: Et hier soir, alors ?
items.en: And last night, then?
items.respell: ay yehr SWAR ah-LOR

items.fr: Ça fait quinze euros soixante, s'il vous plaît.
items.en: That comes to fifteen euros sixty, please.

items.en: That comes to exactly fifty euros.

items.en: That is a bit expensive for me.

items.notes: Un peu is what makes it sayable. C'est cher on its own sounds like a complaint about the shop rather than about your wallet.

items.notes: acheter was never taught here. It came from somewhere else and the modal did not care.

items.fr: Tu peux m'aider ?
items.en: Can you help me?
items.respell: tü PUH meh-DAY
items.notes: Four words, and it works in a shop, a station and a doorway.

items.fr: Donne-moi le dossier.
items.en: Give me the file.
items.respell: donn-mwah luh doh-SYAY

items.fr: Nous devons attendre le bus.
items.en: We have to wait for the bus.
items.respell: noo duh-VOHⁿ ah-TAHⁿ-druh luh BÜS
items.notes: attendre is an -RE verb from lesson 4 in A2 and it does not conjugate here. After a modal, nothing does.

items.fr: Vous voulez choisir ?
items.en: Would you like to choose?
items.respell: voo voo-LAY shwa-ZEER
items.notes: choisir is an -IR verb from lesson 3 in A2, and it arrives here in its dictionary shape.

items.fr: Je bats Paul.
items.en: I beat Paul.
items.respell: zhuh BA POL
items.notes: One t, silent s. Exactly the shape mettre has, on a verb you met a minute ago.

items.fr: Il bat Paul.
items.en: He beats Paul.
items.respell: eel BA POL
items.notes: Three letters, and the same sound as the je form. Nothing to learn that mettre did not give you.

items.fr: Nous battons Paul.
items.en: We beat Paul.
items.respell: noo ba-TOHⁿ POL
items.notes: Two t from here on, and they do not move again. Read it beside nous mettons and nothing is new.

items.fr: J'apprends le français.
items.en: I am learning French.
items.respell: zha-PRAHⁿ luh frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: prends with two letters in front of it. The verb did not change at all.

items.fr: Nous apprenons le français.
items.en: We are learning French.
items.respell: noo-za-pruh-NOHⁿ luh frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: One n, same as nous prenons. The stem does what the head verb does and asks for nothing new.

items.fr: Ils apprennent le français.
items.en: They are learning French.
items.respell: eel-za-PREN luh frahⁿ-SEH
items.notes: Two n, same as ils prennent, and for the same reason: the -ent has no sound in it.

items.fr: Je comprends la question.
items.en: I understand the question.
items.respell: zhuh kohⁿ-PRAHⁿ la kes-TYOHⁿ
items.notes: A different front and the same verb behind it. Four letters added and nothing else touched.

items.fr: Nous comprenons la question.
items.en: We understand the question.
items.respell: noo kohⁿ-pruh-NOHⁿ la kes-TYOHⁿ
items.notes: One n. If you can build nous prenons you have already built this one.

items.fr: Tu réponds vite.
items.en: You answer quickly.
items.respell: tü ray-pohⁿ VEET
items.notes: Spelled exactly like the je form and said exactly like it too.

items.fr: Il répond vite.
items.en: He answers quickly.
items.respell: eel ray-pohⁿ VEET
items.notes: One letter shorter than the other two and said the same way. The bare form on a second verb.

items.fr: Elle attend le bus.
items.en: She is waiting for the bus.
items.respell: e la-tahⁿ luh BÜS
items.notes: The bare form again, and the l of elle moves across onto the verb because attendre begins with a vowel.

items.fr: Ils attendent le bus.
items.en: They are waiting for the bus.
items.respell: eel za-tahⁿd luh BÜS
items.notes: The silent s of ils wakes up in front of the vowel, and the d wakes up in front of the -ent.

items.fr: Il entend le train.
items.en: He can hear the train.
items.respell: ee lahⁿ-tahⁿ luh TRAⁿ
items.notes: Three nasal vowels and not one N sound in the whole sentence.

items.fr: Ils entendent le train.
items.en: They can hear the train.
items.respell: eel zahⁿ-tahⁿd luh TRAⁿ

items.fr: Elle rend le livre.
items.en: She is giving the book back.
items.respell: el rahⁿ luh LEEVR

items.fr: Elles rendent le livre.
items.en: They are giving the book back.
items.respell: el rahⁿd luh LEEVR
items.notes: elle and elles are one sound, so the d at the end of the verb is the only evidence there is.

items.fr: Tu appelles Marie.
items.en: You are calling Marie.
items.respell: tü ah-PEL ma-REE
items.notes: Two l. The doubled consonant is how -eler writes the open è.

items.fr: ralentir
items.en: to slow down
items.respell: rah-lahⁿ-TEER

items.fr: grandir
items.en: to grow up
items.respell: grahⁿ-DEER

example.en: Children grow up fast.
example.fr: Les enfants grandissent vite.

items.fr: guérir
items.en: to heal, to recover
items.respell: gay-REER

example.en: He recovered quickly from his flu.
example.fr: Il a guéri rapidement de sa grippe.

items.fr: Nous les invitons.
items.en: We invite them.
items.respell: noo lay zaⁿ-vee-TOHⁿ
items.notes: The liaison on les is audible before the vowel of invitons.

items.fr: Elle la connaît.
items.en: She knows her.
items.respell: ehl lah koh-NEH
items.notes: Feminine subject and feminine pronoun, and they have nothing to do with each other. The pronoun takes the gender of the noun it stands for.

items.fr: Vous le voyez.
items.en: You see it.
items.respell: voo luh vwah-YAY
items.notes: The vous cell. Nothing about the pronoun responds to the subject changing.

items.fr: montrer
items.en: to show
items.respell: mohⁿ-TRAY
items.notes: regular -er verb

items.fr: Ils répètent la phrase.
items.en: They repeat the sentence.
items.respell: eel ray-PET la FRAZ
items.notes: The -ent is four letters and no sound, so the stem is the last thing heard and the vowel opens.

items.fr: Nous répétons la phrase.
items.en: We repeat the sentence.
items.respell: noo ray-pay-TOHⁿ la FRAZ
items.notes: Same verb, audible ending, closed vowel. The rule is about the ending, not about the verb.

items.fr: Nous appelons Marie.
items.en: We are calling Marie.
items.respell: noo zah-PLOHⁿ ma-REE
items.notes: One l. The ending sounds, so the stem goes back to the spelling the infinitive had.

items.fr: Tu achètes du pain.
items.en: You buy bread.
items.respell: tü ah-SHET dü PAⁿ
items.notes: Same shape of infinitive as appeler, same open è, and an accent instead of a doubled letter.

items.fr: il faudrait
items.en: it would need, we should
items.respell: eel foh-DREH

items.fr: Il parle ici.
items.en: He speaks here.
items.respell: eel parl ee-SEE
items.notes: The -ER third person, from lesson 1 in A2. One letter after the stem, and it is silent.

items.fr: Nous vendons ici.
items.en: We sell here.
items.respell: noo vahⁿ-dohⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: The same -ons as lesson 1 in A2 and lesson 3 in A2, and the d in front of it is said. Out loud most rooms say on vend instead.

items.fr: Vous vendez ici.
items.en: You sell here.
items.respell: voo vahⁿ-day ee-SEE
items.notes: The same -ez, and the d is said in front of it as well.

items.fr: Ils vendent ici.
items.en: They sell here.
items.respell: eel vahⁿd ee-SEE
items.notes: The -ent is silent and the d in front of it is not, so this is the one plural you can hear against Il vend ici.

items.fr: J'ai couru vite.
items.en: I ran fast.
items.respell: ZHAY koo-RÜ VEET
items.notes: AN -IR VERB WHOSE PAST FORM IS NOT -i. Lesson 16 in A2 taught -IR to -i and courir is one of the verbs that refuses it.

items.fr: Vous venez souvent ici ?
items.en: Do you come here often?
items.respell: voo vuh-NAY soo-VAHⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: Her question, and every word in it is one you have had since a1.

items.fr: Oui, je mange souvent ici.
items.en: Yes, I often eat here.
items.respell: wee zhuh MAHⁿZH soo-VAHⁿ ee-SEE
items.notes: Five words, all of them yours, and the only difficulty was which order they go in.

items.fr: évidemment
items.en: obviously
items.respell: ay-vee-da-MAHⁿ
items.notes: évident; -emment is pronounced like -amment

items.fr: constamment
items.en: constantly
items.respell: kohⁿs-ta-MAHⁿ
items.notes: constant + -amment

items.fr: Au Québec, les taxes s'ajoutent à la caisse.
items.en: In Quebec, the taxes are added at the till.

items.respell: oh kay-BEK lay taks sa-ZHOOT a lah KESS
items.notes: The number on the shelf is not the number you pay. No rate is named and no sum is ever asked for.

items.fr: Non, je ne vais pas venir.
items.en: No, I am not going to come.
items.respell: nohⁿ zhuh nuh veh pah vuh-NEER
items.notes: The refusal, in full, which is the sentence the scene never reached.

items.fr: Ils ne vont pas venir à la fête.
items.en: They aren't going to come to the party.
items.ipa: /il nə vɔ̃ pa və.niʁ a la fɛt/
items.respell: eel nuh vohⁿ pah vuh-NEER a la FEHT
items.notes: Vont is easy to confuse with on or ont by sound, so check the subject ils carefully.

items.fr: Ils ont mangé au restaurant.
items.en: They ate at the restaurant.
items.respell: eel zohⁿ mahⁿ-ZHAY oh res-toh-RAHⁿ

items.fr: C'est plutôt une douleur sourde.
items.en: It is more of a dull ache.

items.fr: Ça fait mal ici.
items.en: It hurts here.
items.respell: sa feh mal ee-SEE
items.notes: Four words and a finger. It is the answer to montrez-moi où ça fait mal and it needs no body-part noun at all.

items.fr: Vous pourriez parler un peu plus fort ?
items.en: Could you speak a little louder?
items.ipa: /vu pu.ʁje paʁ.le œ̃ pø ply fɔʁ/
items.respell: voo poo-ryay par-lay uhⁿ puh plü FOR

items.en: No, we have not finished.
items.respell: nohⁿ · noo na-vohⁿ pa fee-NEE
items.notes: The nous negative, where the ne shortens and takes the liaison with it. Twenty letters, so it is not a dictée target.

items.fr: J'ai couvert le plat.
items.en: I covered the dish.

items.fr: J'ai beaucoup souffert.
items.en: I suffered a lot.
items.respell: ZHAY boh-KOO soo-FEHR
items.notes: The fourth and last member, with lesson 16 in A2's adverb sitting in the gap where that lesson put it.

items.fr: J'ai été malade.
items.en: I was ill.
items.respell: ZHAY ay-TAY ma-LAD
items.notes: From nowhere. There is no route from être to été, and the same three letters are also the word for summer.

items.fr: J'ai eu peur.
items.en: I was frightened.
items.respell: ZHAY Ü PUHR

items.fr: Il est né ici.
items.en: He was born here.
items.respell: eel eh NAY ee-SEE

items.en: She took an exam.

items.respell: ehl eh NAY ee-SEE

items.fr: dans dix minutes

items.fr: Tu es ici depuis longtemps ?
items.en: Have you been here long?
items.respell: tü eh ee-SEE duh-PWEE lohⁿ-TAHⁿ
items.notes: Her question, and every word in it is one the learner has had since a1.

items.fr: Il pleut pendant deux heures.
items.en: It rains for two hours.
items.respell: eel PLEU pahⁿ-DAHⁿ duh ZUHR
items.notes: The same weather as row 177 and the other word, so the pair differs by one thing. Here the rain stops.

items.fr: en deux heures
items.en: in two hours, that is how long it took
items.respell: AHⁿ duh ZUHR
items.notes: Twelve letters, and the shortest thing in the lesson. Same two hours as pendant and depuis, and a third answer.

items.respell: luh FEELM ko-MAHⁿS dAHⁿ zün UHR

items.notes: What he says. It is not wrong and it is not a sentence, and the pause in front of it is the whole cost of the lesson.

items.respell: duh-PWEE duh-ZAHⁿ · ay TWAH
items.notes: The answer with no verb in it, which is what people say, and the question straight back.

items.fr: Je voudrais juste vérifier une chose.

items.respell: zhuh voo-dreh zhüst vay-ree-fyay ün SHOHZ

items.respell: noo noo ruh-poh-ZOHⁿ luh SWAHR

items.fr: Je m'habille vite.

items.respell: zhuh mah-BEEY VEET
items.notes: THE PRONOUN ELIDES. me becomes m before a vowel, which is sons.07s rule arriving on a word the learner now has to choose.

items.fr: Ils s'habillent vite.
items.en: They get dressed quickly.
items.respell: eel sah-BEEY VEET

items.notes: Role play turn 1.

items.respell: noo noo luh-VOHⁿ ah lah mem UHR
items.notes: Role play turn 3. The doubled form produced rather than read.

items.notes: Role play turn 4. The negative, on a verb the paradigm never carried.

items.respell: ehl seh bro-SAY lay DAHⁿ

items.fr: Elle a lavé la voiture.

items.respell: ehl ah lah-VAY lah vwah-TÜR

items.fr: Il ne s'est pas levé.

items.respell: eel nuh seh pah luh-VAY
items.notes: The same again in the third person. Fifteen letters, and the dictée runs it against the affirmative.

items.fr: Elle ne s'est pas levée.
items.en: She did not get up.
items.respell: ehl nuh seh pah luh-VAY
items.notes: THE ENDING SITS OUTSIDE THE WRAP and goes on exactly as it would without one. Eighteen letters, so it is not dictated.

items.fr: Nous ne nous sommes pas levés.

items.respell: noo nuh noo somm pah luh-VAY

items.fr: Elle s'est habillée.
items.en: She got dressed.
items.respell: ehl seh tah-bee-YAY
items.notes: s habiller, built rather than shown, and the ending is on it. Sixteen letters exactly.

items.fr: Nous nous sommes dépêchés.
items.en: We hurried.
items.respell: noo noo somm day-peh-SHAY
items.notes: Nobody hurries themselves and it takes être anyway, because the little word is there. Lesson 19 in A2 taught that this one means nothing by it.

items.fr: Vous vous êtes reposés.

items.respell: voo voo zeht ruh-poh-ZAY

items.fr: Ils se sont douchés.

items.respell: eel suh sohⁿ doo-SHAY
items.notes: Sixteen letters, so the dictée can ask for the plural ending on a verb that was never conjugated on a screen.

items.fr: Je me suis réveillé à sept heures.

items.respell: zhuh muh swee ray-veh-YAY ah seh TUHR

items.fr: Elle s'est levée.
items.en: She got up.
items.respell: ehl seh luh-VAY
items.notes: Thirteen letters, and the one the dictée uses to ask for the e on the verb the six-person walk ran on.

items.fr: Ils ne se sont pas levés.

items.fr: Je ne leur parle pas.

items.fr: Il ne lui répond pas.

items.fr: Le plat est froid.

items.respell: luh PLA eh FRWA
